title: Şirince Village Guide: Stone Houses, Wine & Proximity to Ephesus
metaDescription: Şirince is a hillside stone-house village 11 km (15 to 20 minutes by car) from the Ephesus Archaeological Site.
quickAnswer: Şirince is a hillside stone-house village 11 km (15 to 20 minutes by car) from the Ephesus Archaeological Site. Staying overnight lets you enjoy quiet mornings and wood-fired dinners after day-trip buses leave at 17:00, sample cold-pressed Aegean olive oil and dry grape wines, and reach İzmir Adnan Menderes Airport in about 60 minutes.

body.text: How far is Şirince from Ephesus ruins?

Şirince sits 8 km uphill east of Selçuk town and roughly 11 km from the lower gate of Ephesus—a 15-to-20-minute drive along a winding olive-grove road. You can easily stay in Şirince, reach Ephesus at its 08:00 opening ahead of cruise-ship groups from Kuşadası, and return for a late lunch.

[Ephesus](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1018/), a UNESCO World Heritage site preserving the Library of Celsus, Great Theatre, and Roman Terrace Houses, is managed by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism. Check seasonal hours on the [official Ephesus page on muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?DistId=EFS&SectionId=EFS01): summer hours typically run 08:00–19:00 and winter hours 08:00–18:00, with foreign-visitor entry priced at €40 in 2026 (including the Ephesus Experience Museum, while Terrace Houses require a separate ticket unless covered by [MuseumPass Türkiye](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-27-009)). Frequent dolmuş minibuses run between Şirince and Selçuk bus station every 20 to 30 minutes, where you can connect to Ephesus in five minutes.

body.text: Why is staying overnight in Şirince quieter than visiting at midday?

Between 11:00 and 16:30, Şirince's narrow cobblestone main lane fills with day-trippers and coach groups moving between souvenir stalls. By 17:30 the buses depart, leaving woodsmoke, church bells, and hillside terraces to overnight guests staying in restored 19th-century Ottoman-Greek stone houses.

Sleeping in Şirince transforms the village from a noisy shopping alley into a peaceful Aegean retreat. Mornings before 09:30 are ideal for walking up to the restored Church of St. John the Baptist and the upper residential lanes where laundry lines hang between peach orchards. Choose a stone guesthouse slightly above the main bazaar street—away from the lower parking lot—for quiet nights and valley views. What local olive oils and fruit wines are authentic vs touristy?

Şirince is famous for fruit wines (blackberry, mulberry, melon, and peach), yet most brightly labelled bottles sold along the main lane are sweetened, mass-bottled blends aimed at quick tastings. For authentic Aegean produce, seek out small-batch dry grape wines from nearby Urla or local estate vineyards, and cold-pressed early-harvest olive oil milled in Selçuk.

Taste before buying and check the label rather than relying on street-side free-pour pitches. Authentic natürel sızma (extra-virgin) olive oil from the surrounding hills carries a peppery finish and a harvest date from the most recent October–December pressing. For wine, ask for dry Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, or indigenous Turkish Bornova Misketi and Öküzgözü rather than syrupy fruit infusions.

items: Look for "Erken Hasat Soğuk Sıkım" (early-harvest, cold-pressed) and the current harvest year on olive oil tins.
Taste dry estate grape wines alongside any fruit wine so you can compare acidity and sweetness.
Buy handmade olive-oil soap from small village workshops without synthetic neon dyes or heavy perfume.
Skip street-front stalls pushing "organic" labels without producer names or batch dates.

body.text: How do you reach Şirince from İzmir Airport?

Driving or taking a pre-arranged transfer from İzmir Adnan Menderes Airport (ADB) to Şirince takes 55 to 70 minutes (roughly 68 km) via the O-31 motorway south to Selçuk. By rail, board the İZBAN suburban train directly at the airport terminal, transfer at Tepeköy to the Selçuk branch, and take a 15-minute taxi or dolmuş uphill to Şirince.

Check live departures on the [official İZBAN timetable page](https://www.izban.com.tr/sayfalar/SeferSaatleri.aspx?MenuId=22) before landing; the airport-to-Selçuk rail leg takes roughly 65 to 75 minutes including the platform change at Tepeköy. Carry a small amount of Turkish lira cash for the Selçuk–Şirince dolmuş, as minibuses rarely accept foreign cards. faq.q: How many nights should I spend in Şirince?
faq.a: One to two nights is ideal. Two nights gives you a full morning at Ephesus, an afternoon at the Ephesus Archaeological Museum in Selçuk, and two relaxed evenings in Şirince without rushing.

faq.q: Can you drive a rental car into Şirince village?
faq.a: Private cars are restricted from entering the narrow cobblestone core. Park in the municipal lots at the village entrance and walk 5 to 10 minutes uphill to your guesthouse; most boutique inns assist with luggage on request.

faq.q: Is Şirince suitable for travellers with limited mobility?
faq.a: The main lower lane is gently sloped, but most historic stone houses and hillside viewpoints require climbing steep, uneven cobblestones and stairs. Travellers with mobility constraints should choose a lower-elevation stay near the village entrance or base in flat Selçuk.

faq.q: Can you visit Nesin Mathematics Village from Şirince?
faq.a: Yes, Nesin Mathematics Village sits about 1.5 km outside Şirince along a pleasant country road. Visitor hours and campus access depend on active student camps, so check local schedules before walking over.

faq.q: Are Şirince fruit wines good quality?
faq.a: They are light, sweet, low-tannin dessert-style drinks best enjoyed chilled on a terrace, though quality varies sharply between producers. For serious wine tasting, pair Şirince with a half-day drive to the Urla Vineyard Route west of İzmir.

faq.q: When is the best time of year to visit Şirince and Ephesus?
faq.a: April to early June and late September to November offer warm days, active olive harvests in autumn, and far gentler temperatures inside the exposed marble ruins of Ephesus than July or August.
